summary.headline: Divis Labs Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 32% YoY to Rs 3,770 crore and PAT rose 64% to Rs 1,127 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated total income was Rs 3,770 crore (up ~32% YoY) with PBT of Rs 1,505 crore (up 65%) and PAT of Rs 1,127 crore (up ~64%). For H1, total income reached Rs 6,907 crore (vs Rs 5,389 crore) and PAT Rs 2,029 crore (vs Rs 1,234 crore). Management said demand and volumes were healthy, though pricing pressure persists in some categories and input and logistics costs are elevated due to Middle East disruption. Management reiterated guidance of double-digit revenue growth but declined to quantify validation-batch contribution, peptide capacity or margin guidance.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 5,389 crore in H1 FY26
vs Rs 103 crore gain in H1 FY26

segments.name: Custom synthesis (CDMO)
segments.commentary: Accounted for 62% of H1 sales revenue; management said it grew around 50% YoY in H1 with validation batches cited as a driver, but did not quantify base business growth or margin.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Contributed 38% of H1 sales revenue; no product-level detail given beyond stated mix.

segments.name: Nutraceuticals
segments.commentary: H1 revenue of Rs 571 crore vs Rs 492 crore in H1 FY26 (~16% growth).

segments.name: Peptides
segments.commentary: Vertically integrated from building blocks to dipeptides, tripeptides and large fragments; several 3,000-litre SPPS lines being installed; peptides are for innovator programs only, no generic peptides.

guidance_outlook: Management guided to double-digit revenue growth as the way forward, declining to specify whether H2 would be 10% or 20%.
Management declined to give EBITDA margin guidance when asked whether the 32-35% range would be raised.
Three dedicated CDMO projects are closer to commercialisation: one within the next few quarters, the other two in the next one to two quarters.
Capex run-rate expected at about Rs 2,000 crore plus or minus 20% per year over the next two to three years, based on current RFPs; not split by segment.
capex_capacity: CWIP of Rs 1,638 crore at 30 Sep 2026; H1 capitalisation Rs 1,223 crore including Rs 772 crore in Q2.
Installing several 3,000-litre SPPS lines for peptide programs; management said it expects to be among the top three SPPS players in future.
Three major dedicated capex programs in validation; dedicated facilities with specialised equipment used only for their products.
Multi-purpose blocks: Unit 1 about 22, Unit 2 about 25, Unit 3 about 6 production blocks; only three blocks dedicated.
Flow chemistry and bio-catalysis platforms being expanded; UNICHEM Kakinada cited for backward integration and pre-chemistry.
demand_pricing: Pricing pressure persists in certain product categories, but volumes grew healthily across the business.
Input costs elevated, particularly petrochemical solvents; management said suppliers are also facing cost increases.
Logistics costs and transit times higher due to Red Sea and Suez disruption and air freight constraints.
Company maintains rolling three-month inventory cover for critical materials.
Management said RFPs are increasing and customer interest in peptides and custom synthesis is growing.
Management said about 60 to 70 projects are at various stages from pre-chemistry to commercial.

qa_highlights.question: What is base business growth and margin excluding validation batches in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify validation revenue or base business growth and margin, saying validation work is an ongoing part of the customer pipeline that leads to commercialisation.

qa_highlights.question: Will the agency inspection be required before commercial batches start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no inspection notice has been received yet; the agency may clear the file based on past history or require a pre-approval inspection, to be known once customers submit batches.

qa_highlights.question: Why has cost containment helped gross margin while volumes grew about 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited wider supplier cost inflation, but attributed the material cost ratio drop from 40% to 32% to a higher CDMO mix and backward integration at Unit 1 and Kakinada.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a generic-entry risk on a top product in Europe, and is lifecycle management under way?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it could not comment on specific products or customers, and that the product could have gone generic.

qa_highlights.question: Why has operating cash flow lagged PAT growth in H1?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO before tax was about Rs 9.59 crore for H1; management attributed it to the large capex cycle, with about Rs 870 crore of work in progress and advances to suppliers.

qa_highlights.question: How much capex is planned for the next few years and how is it allocated?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 2,000 crore plus or minus 20% per year, based on RFPs; segment-wise split not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company adding liquid-phase peptide capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid-phase is a well-established capability, and that pilot-scale capacity can be scaled as needed; no major liquid-phase expansion was described.

qa_highlights.question: Will a bonus issue be considered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a board decision and that it would be communicated by the board when appropriate.

risks_watch: Validation-batch revenue is unquantified; base business growth and margins are not disclosed, so H2 sustainability is unclear.
Timing of regulatory inspection or approval for the three dedicated CDMO projects is unknown.
Working capital and CFO are lagging PAT growth, with inventories at Rs 5,325 crore and receivables at Rs 3,705 crore.
Generic entry for a top product in Europe, with LOE reported as around November 2026; management declined to comment.
Middle East disruption continues to affect solvent prices, freight and transit times.
Forex turned to a Rs 20 crore loss in H1 vs a Rs 103 crore gain last year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and customer interest, but evasive on quantification: management repeatedly declined to split validation revenue, product-level details, peptide capacity, segment capex and margin guidance.
key_quotes: So it's very difficult for me to quantify all I can say the CS business and how we must express CS business and the generic business as about 62% of CS.
As I said earlier, the guidance would be revenue growing at double digit growth rate and I cannot comment more than that at this point.
So the CPEX is divided uniformly between all the three units and we have been investing actively into several new technologies in flow chemistry.

growth.why: Management guided only to double-digit revenue growth for H2 FY27 with no figure, while Q2 total income rose 32% YoY and PAT 64%; backing is partial, citing three dedicated CDMO projects nearing commercialisation within 1-2 quarters, 60-70 projects in pipeline, rising RFPs, and ~Rs 2,000 crore annual capex, but no capacity volumes or order values were quantified.
